quarterly_data.signal: CFO Henriette Wennicke (H1 2026 call): H1 2026 revenue was DKK 4.5 billion, driven by recognition of the DKK 3.7 billion phase III initiation development milestone and the DKK 798 million first anniversary payment under the Roche collaboration and licensing agreement (the milestone cash is received when the study actually starts); operating expenses DKK 1.2 billion, mostly R&D; net financial items a positive DKK 292 million; profit DKK 3.5 billion; cash position DKK 14.5 billion at the end of June.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 revenue DKK 4.5 billion; profit DKK 3.5 billion; cash DKK 14.5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Henriette Wennicke: no change to 2026 financial guidance - collaboration revenue of DKK 4.5 billion and operating expenses of DKK 2.7 billion to DKK 3.3 billion, mainly driven by R&D.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 collaboration revenue DKK 4.5 billion; opex DKK 2.7 billion to DKK 3.3 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline milestones (H1 2026 call): CMO David Kendall said Zealand and Roche decided to advance petrelintide monotherapy into a phase III registrational program on track to start later this year (CEO Adam Steensberg: 'full speed ahead'); topline phase II ZUPREME 2 results (about 200 adults with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes, three doses vs placebo over 28 weeks) are due in the second half; the phase II ZYNERGY trial of petrelintide with Roche's GLP-1/GIP agonist anasepatide (six arms, separate injections, primary endpoint at week 40) is starting, to inform a single-cartridge co-formulated combination in phase III; a phase Ib trial of Kv1.3 blocker ZP9830 in about 30 plaque-psoriasis patients (eight weeks) has started, with multiple-ascending-dose topline later this year; a first-in-human trial of GIP agonist ZP6590 has started; glepaglutide's phase III EASE 5 trial progresses and the EASE 2 / EASE 3 extensions are complete, with data at congresses in 2027; partner Boehringer Ingelheim's SYNCHRONIZE-2 and SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT survodutide readouts are expected this year.
quarterly_data.figure: ZUPREME 2 about 200 adults, 28 weeks; ZP9830 phase Ib about 30 participants

quarterly_data.signal: Clinical data (H1 2026 call, CMO David Kendall): in ZUPREME-1 petrelintide delivered double-digit weight loss with no apparent plateau over 42 weeks; more than three-quarters of GI events were mild and transient, mostly during dose escalation, and up to 98% of participants reached their target maintenance dose; even the 1 and 2.5 milligram doses gave near double-digit weight loss. For partner Boehringer Ingelheim's survodutide, the 76-week SYNCHRONIZE-1 trial gave up to 16.6% weight loss vs 3.2% on placebo, with an MRI sub-study showing up to a 34% reduction in visceral fat and a 63% reduction in liver fat content and lean mass no more than 11.3% of tissue lost at the highest dose; in the 48-week SYNCHRONIZE-MASLD trial 6 out of 10 participants achieved liver fat normalization with mean weight loss of up to 12%. Boehringer Ingelheim expanded the program with four new phase IIIb trials in 2026 using more flexible titration.
quarterly_data.figure: survodutide up to 16.6% weight loss; visceral fat up to 34% lower; liver fat 63% lower

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Adam Steensberg (H1 2026 call), management view on the obesity market: with GLP-1s about 30% of patients have dropped off after 3 months and only 20% are still on treatment after a year; about 80% of patients in Zealand's surveys look for weight loss below 20%; he expects obesity treatment to become a 'weight loss journey' starting with a tolerable therapy such as petrelintide and stepping up to combinations only when needed. He said Zealand has not heard of illegal, compounded or imported use of petrelintide. Strategy: external innovation through platform collaborations such as OTR Therapeutics (small molecules), partnering autoimmune programs such as Kv1.3 with established players, and a royalty-rights sale of the non-strategic asset rusfertide to Royalty Pharma announced the day before the call.
